name: Multi-hypothesis heads: Mixture Density Networks (Bishop 1994), Multiple Choice Learning / winner-takes-all (Guzman-Rivera 2012, sMCL Lee 2016, relaxed WTA Rupprecht 2017, EWTA Makansi 2019, MTP loss Cui 2019), resilient MCL with learned scoring heads (rMCL, NeurIPS 2023), WTA-as-density-estimator (ICML 2024), annealed MCL (aMCL, NeurIPS 2024), TimeMCL (2025)
authors_org: MDN: C. Bishop (Aston, 1994). rMCL / WTA-density / aMCL / TimeMCL: V. Letzelter, D. Perera, M. Fontaine, M. Chen, P. Perez, S. Essid, G. Richard, A. Cortes and co-authors (LTCI Telecom Paris, Valeo.ai). Relaxed WTA: Rupprecht et al. (TUM). EWTA: Makansi et al. (Freiburg). MTP: Cui et al. (Uber ATG).
venue_link: aMCL: NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.15580 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15580). rMCL: NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2311.01052 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01052). WTA learners are geometry-aware conditional density estimators: ICML 2024, PMLR 235:27254-27287 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/letzelter24a.html, arXiv:2406.04706). TimeMCL: arXiv:2506.05515 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05515). Relaxed WTA: ICCV 2017 'Learning in an Uncertain World'. EWTA: CVPR 2019 'Overcoming Limitations of Mixture Density Networks'. MTP: ICRA 2019 (arXiv:1809.10732).
code_availability: Public PyTorch code: github.com/Victorletzelter/annealed_mcl (aMCL), github.com/Victorletzelter/timeMCL (TimeMCL); rMCL code linked from the paper [uncertain]; MTP loss re-implemented by Alyaev (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6531534). MDN / WTA losses are ~30 lines and trivial to reimplement.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (NeurIPS 2023/2024, ICML 2024, ICCV/CVPR/ICRA). aMCL full text read (HTML); rMCL and WTA-density read at abstract level; TimeMCL arXiv preprint read. No application to geosteering except Alyaev et al. 2022 (see A09).
extreme_summary: Predict K hypotheses (plus K scores) in one forward pass and train only the closest one (winner-takes-all), optionally softened by a temperature annealed to zero (aMCL) or by epsilon-relaxation. The hypotheses become an optimal K-point quantization of the conditional distribution, and learned scoring heads (rMCL) turn them into a Voronoi-cell density whose score-weighted mean estimates the conditional mean.
task_definition: Generic ambiguous regression: given x, output a set of plausible y values (sound-source directions, speech sources, future trajectories, time-series futures) instead of one averaged y. Applied to our task: given the lateral/typewell cost image, output K whole-lateral TVT curves (band hypotheses) plus the probability of each.
inputs: Method-agnostic; it is an output head. In our setting it reuses the ConvNeXt/FastViT U-Net features over the 16-channel 345 MD x 400 TVT cost image (GR diffs, trajectory, typewell, prefix channels).
target_parameterisation: Each hypothesis is a vector in output space. For us: K curves of 345 TVT values, preferably parameterised as offsets from the known heel TVT or from the per-column expectation so different hypotheses correspond to different bands. MDN alternative: per-column Gaussian mixture over TVT, which our 400-bin softmax already subsumes.
output_representation: K hypotheses f_1..f_K(x) plus K scores gamma_k(x) summing to one (rMCL/aMCL), or for MDN K means, K widths and K mixture weights. rMCL interprets the pair as a piecewise-constant density over the Voronoi cells of the hypotheses; ICML 2024 adds kernel-smoothed Voronoi densities for NLL evaluation.
architecture: Shared backbone -> K hypothesis heads (linear or small MLP each) + one scoring head with K logits (softmax or K sigmoids). TimeMCL puts K heads on a TimeGrad-style RNN encoder and outputs K whole multivariate trajectories. MTP (Cui 2019; Alyaev 2022) concatenates K trajectories and K logits in one vector. For our U-Net: pool decoder features along the TVT axis (e.g. posterior-weighted pooling) to one feature per MD column, a 1D conv/transformer along MD, K curve heads (345 values each) and a globally pooled K-logit head.
core_mechanism: Winner-takes-all: the loss is min_k l(f_k(x), y), so each head specialises on a region of output space and the heads converge to a centroidal Voronoi tessellation (conditional K-means) of p(y|x) rather than collapsing to the mean. Known failure: hypothesis collapse (some heads never win). Fixes: relaxed WTA (epsilon weight on losers, but it biases hypotheses toward the barycenter), EWTA (top-n winners evolving from n=K to 1), and aMCL: soft Boltzmann assignment q_k ~ exp(-l_k/T) with T annealed to 0 (deterministic annealing); hypotheses split at critical temperatures (first split at T = 2*lambda_max of the conditional covariance), following the rate-distortion curve and avoiding greedy local minima. rMCL: scoring heads trained with binary cross-entropy on 'this head won', giving calibrated cell probabilities; conditional-mean estimator = sum_k gamma_k f_k.
training_objective: WTA: min_k ||f_k - y||^2 plus a scoring loss (CE/BCE on the winner index). aMCL: sum_k softmin_T(l)_k * l_k with the assignment detached, temperature schedule T(t) decaying to 0, plus scoring loss. Relaxed WTA: (1-eps) on the winner + eps/(K-1) on others. MDN: Gaussian-mixture negative log-likelihood (prone to mode collapse and numerical instability, the motivation for EWTA). Use L2 (not L1) per hypothesis so each cell converges to its conditional mean, which is what pooled RMSE needs.
decoding: (i) score-weighted mean sum_k gamma_k f_k (conditional-mean estimate); (ii) argmax-score hypothesis (mode-seeking); (iii) pass all K hypotheses + scores to a reranker/gate that uses extra evidence and outputs new weights, then take the reweighted mean. Papers report distortion (min over hypotheses, an oracle) and RMSE of the weighted mean.
metric_consistent_decode: Only the score-weighted (or reweighted) mean is RMSE-consistent. Picking the top-scored hypothesis is mode-seeking and will raise pooled RMSE unless the selector is far more accurate than the posterior (the same reason arg-max lost to the expectation in our repo). Oracle 'distortion' numbers in MCL papers are not achievable metrics.
evidence_scope: Whatever the backbone sees; for us the whole lateral plus typewell (U-Net receptive field), single well. A reranker on top can add whole-lateral path-level evidence.
prefix_conditioning: Not part of the method. Hypotheses can be anchored to the last known heel TVT (offset parameterisation); prefix channels already enter the backbone.
propose_vs_select: Propose-and-score in one pass. The K hypotheses are an explicit candidate set, so it slots into a propose + rerank/gate pipeline (like 3rd place's five candidates + softmax gate, or 2nd place's sampled rollouts + shape-gate top-k average).
physical_constraints: None intrinsic. Each hypothesis is a whole path, so it can be regularised (smoothness / dS curvature, start at known TVT, near-linear drift), which is impossible for per-column marginals.
dataset: UCI regression, WSJ0-mix speech separation (aMCL), sound-event localisation (rMCL), GluonTS Solar/Electricity/Exchange/Traffic/Taxi/Wikipedia (TimeMCL), vehicle trajectories (MTP/EWTA). In-domain: Alyaev 2022 on the GWC 2020 synthetic typelog (A09).
synthetic_to_real: Not addressed. WTA learns diversity from the spread of targets among similar-looking inputs; our 85% synthetic generator provides this at scale for repeated-layer cases, but scores learned on synthetic data may be miscalibrated on real wells.
metric_and_performance: aMCL: WSJ0-2mix SI-SDR 16.85+-0.13 vs PIT 16.88+-0.10; 3-mix 10.00 vs 10.01, lower seed variance than MCL; UCI RMSE comparable to relaxed WTA and competitive with MC-dropout / deep ensembles. TimeMCL: distortion on par with TimeGrad/TACTiS-2 at orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs, smoother trajectories. rMCL: better calibrated than MCL for sound-source localisation. None report RMSE gains of the weighted-mean decode over a strong density model; the wins are in distortion (oracle-of-K) and multimodal fidelity.
comparability: Not comparable; no geosteering numbers. The relevant internal ceiling is our oracle best-mode decode 4.27 ft vs 4.84 ft deployed (a perfect selector over per-column modes).
validation_protocol: Standard fixed splits; multiple seeds reported for aMCL. Not applicable to our well-level holdout.
inference_budget: Negligible: K extra heads on the existing backbone (well under 1 ms). A reranker scoring K paths with a GR-misfit integral is O(K x columns) on CPU. Fits the Kaggle/rig budget.
repeated_layers: Exactly the target case: each repeated band can be owned by one hypothesis, so the model states 'band A with prob p, band B with prob 1-p' as two coherent whole paths instead of a per-column blend. WTA pressure rewards committing a head to a band, removing hedged blends inside a head (our blend error, 15%). The mixture still carries the ambiguity; RMSE drops only if the scores (or a reranker) are better calibrated than today's softmax band weights.
drift: Indirect. Hypotheses are whole curves, so heads can represent 'same band, different slope', a quantization of drift uncertainty. Adds no evidence against drift by itself.
uncertainty_and_calibration: rMCL scores are trained as winner probabilities and reported better calibrated than vanilla MCL; aMCL reduces collapse. Hypothesis-level calibration can be checked with a reliability diagram of 'hypothesis k won' over holdout wells and fixed by temperature scaling of score logits. Our current calibration is only per bin.
where_to_use: Auxiliary head on the ConvNeXt/FastViT U-Net decoder (experiments/arch/seq_NN_models.py, seq_NN_trf_unet.py) trained jointly with the existing column cross-entropy; its K paths + scores feed a whole-lateral reranker that outputs reweighted scores; final prediction = reweighted mean, blended with the existing expectation.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%: wrong_mode 24%, blend 15%, multimodal_miss 12%); secondarily drift via slope hypotheses.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Today the ConvNeXt outputs per-column marginals only (400-bin softmax, expectation decode); nothing represents a joint whole-lateral hypothesis, and the loss (alignment soft CE + expectation regression + GR_penalty; unet_loss_weights in experiments/arch/seq_NN_cfg.py / seq_NN_train.py) has no diversity or path-coherence term. Consequences: (1) we cannot assign a probability to 'the well is in band B along the whole lateral', so evidence visible only at path level (integrated GR misfit of the entire path, linearity of drift, consistency with the prefix) never reaches the weights; our failed per-point gates and XY prior acted at point level. (2) Per-column MDN/MCL is NOT a gap: a 400-bin softmax is already a more flexible per-column density. (3) The 2nd-place code already does a stochastic propose + rerank (rollout_paths samples paths from the AnchorCNN move field, then averages the top-k by shape distance to a reference MLP), but its proposals come from a weaker model (AnchorCNN 5.94 ft holdout). (4) Theory: with a calibrated mixture, the score-weighted mean of K WTA hypotheses and our expectation both estimate E[y|x], so an MCL head alone cannot beat a calibrated softmax on pooled RMSE; any gain must come from path-level evidence used by a reranker, or from the auxiliary training signal improving the shared backbone.
proposed_experiment: E0 (no training, go/no-go, ~1 h CPU): from posterior_all.npz (seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all) extract K=2-4 coherent paths per well by tracking per-column modes, or by forward-filtering-backward-sampling many paths (reuse posterior_fb_decode.py) and k-means clustering them. Report (a) path-oracle RMSE vs point-oracle 4.27 vs expectation; (b) path-level soft reweighting: w_k proportional to mass_k * exp(-beta * integrated GR misfit of path k against the typewell over the unknown suffix - beta2 * linear-drift residual), beta fitted on TRAINING wells only; decode = sum_k w_k path_k, blended with the expectation. Keep only if the pooled gain on the 155 holdout wells exceeds the +-0.39 ft noise floor. E1 (training): add mhyp_k (4/6), mhyp_lambda (0.1/0.3), mhyp_mode ('amcl' with T0 ~ 25 ft^2 decaying to 0 over the first 60% of epochs, or 'rwta' eps=0.05) to seq_NN_cfg.py; head in seq_NN_models.py: posterior-weighted TVT pooling of decoder features -> 1D conv along MD -> K offset curves from the heel TVT + K score logits; loss in seq_NN_train.py: masked L2 per hypothesis over unknown columns with aMCL soft assignment + CE scoring loss, added as a new unet_loss_weights key. Evaluate with seq_NN_holdout_eval.py: (i) expectation of the unchanged softmax (does the auxiliary loss help the backbone?), (ii) score-weighted mean of paths, (iii) E0 reranker on learned paths, (iv) 50/50 blends. Control: identical config with mhyp_lambda=0, same seed, 150 epochs; 2 seeds per arm because of the noise floor. Log hypothesis-collapse rate and score reliability.
implementation_effort: Medium: head and loss are small, but path parameterisation, masking of variable-length suffixes, the annealing schedule and the reranker need care. E0 alone is low effort.
gpu_cost: Head adds <2% FLOPs; E1 costs one extra 150-epoch ConvNeXt-small run plus its control, the same as any normal run on the RTX 5060 8 GB (several hours each) [uncertain]. E0 is CPU only.
distillation_compatibility: Compatible. Either give the FastViT student the same head and distil scores by KL and hypotheses by L2 after Hungarian matching of teacher/student heads (heads are permutation-ambiguous), or keep KD on per-column posteriors as today and let the student learn its own heads. The existing per-column KD path is unaffected.
error_correlation_with_ours: High correlation if used as a weighted mean (same backbone, same information). Diversity comes only from the reranker's path-level evidence, so it is a gate/reweighting component rather than an independent blend member.
risk: (1) Metric: any hard selection is mode-seeking; our continuity decode and arg-max both lost for this reason, so only soft reweighting is safe. (2) Selection overfitting: 3rd place's gate had CV 5.29 vs private 5.84, and our learned per-point gates were rejected (5.017 vs 4.905 for one weight). (3) Data-limited: only 618 real training wells to calibrate path scores. (4) Collapse and temperature-schedule sensitivity (a stated aMCL limitation, tied to the LR). (5) If the path oracle is barely below 4.27 or GR-misfit reweighting does not beat the softmax weights, the band information is not in the data and no head will help.
notes: In-domain precedent: Alyaev et al. 2022 (A09) used MTP best-of-M on the same kind of GR difference image (M=7) and reported mostly oracle-level wins. The ICML 2024 result (WTA hypotheses + scores form a Voronoi conditional density) is the formal reason the weighted-mean decode cannot beat a calibrated softmax by itself. aMCL is the most robust training choice (lower seed variance, no barycenter bias); prefer it over relaxed WTA. A trained CRF (item B05) with forward-filtering-backward-sampling is a training-free generator of coherent path hypotheses and could replace the learned head as the proposal stage.
